title: Water, plumbing and gas boundaries
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Plumbing, draining and gasfitting (last updated 31 July 2026; page metadata shows a later modified date); Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC), When you need a QBCC licence (last reviewed 11 August 2021); Building and Plumbing Commission (Victoria), Gasfitting work (last updated 30 June 2026); Energy Safe Victoria, Gas emergencies (reviewed 29 January 2023); Jemena, Gas safety (no last-updated or publication date shown; footer copyright 2026); Jemena, Jemena Gas Networks (no last-updated date shown; footer copyright 2026); Queensland Government, Gas safety (last updated 3 September 2026); APA (Allgas network), Information for Brisbane, South Gold Coast, Toowoomba and Oakey customers (no last-updated date shown).
audience: Handyman workers and property maintenance workers who may encounter water, drainage or gas systems
learningOutcomes: Identify the water, drainage and gas tasks that are referred to a licensed plumber or gasfitter.
Respond safely to a leak, a suspected gas smell or a blocked drain found during other work.
State the licence positions for plumbing, drainage and gasfitting in each state, without implying authority to perform the work.

instruction.heading: What counts as plumbing, drainage and gas work
instruction.body: Plumbing and drainage work includes installing, altering, repairing and removing water supply pipes, fixtures connected to them, and drainage lines. Gas work includes gas appliances, gas pipes and their connections. Some everyday tasks sit close to these boundaries: changing a tap washer, fitting a shower head, clearing a blocked drain, or fitting a flexible hose to a gas appliance. Do not assume that a small change is outside the licence. Check the state position first, and refer when it is unclear.

instruction.heading: The licence picture by state
instruction.body: In New South Wales, a licence or certificate is needed for plumbing, draining or gasfitting work at any price, by category (NSW plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). In Queensland, a QBCC licence is needed for plumbing, drainage and gasfitting at any dollar value (QBCC page, last reviewed 11 August 2021). In Victoria, gasfitting covers work on items, and the definition excludes cleaning, painting or preparing gas pipes unless the work connects, disconnects or alters them (BPC page, last updated 30 June 2026).

instruction.heading: Everyday water and gas tasks by state
instruction.body:
Four everyday tasks sit on these boundaries: changing a tap washer, fitting a shower head, clearing a blocked drain, and fitting a flexible hose to a gas appliance. They are taught here so that you can recognise them and apply the state rule. Each state note below is a requirement, not a permission. One line per task and state:
- Tap washer and shower head, NSW: the water plumbing category covers work connected with supplying or conveying water, including fittings, and the page does not name tap washers or shower heads. UNCONFIRMED: that this task must be done by a licensed worker in New South Wales.
- Tap washer and shower head, QLD: a QBCC licence is needed for plumbing at any value, and the handyman exemption for work at or under $3,300 does not cover plumbing work. UNCONFIRMED: that this task must be done by a licensed worker in Queensland.
- Tap washer and shower head, VIC: the cited gasfitting page does not cover water plumbing, so the Victorian position for this task is not confirmed in this lesson and it must be referred.
- Blocked drain, NSW: draining covers sanitary drainage connected to a sewer (UNCONFIRMED: this scope is not checked against the NSW page in this review), and a licence or certificate is needed at any cost, so this work must be done by a licensed worker in New South Wales.
- Blocked drain, QLD: a QBCC licence is needed for drainage at any value, so this work must be done by a licensed worker in Queensland.
- Blocked drain, VIC: the drainage position is not confirmed in the cited sources, so it must be referred.
- Flexible gas hose, NSW: gasfitting covers connecting or disconnecting gas appliances, so this work must be done by a licensed worker. UNCONFIRMED exclusion: connections where the point of connection is a gas outlet socket are not gasfitting work. Confirm this with the NSW regulator before relying on it.
- Flexible gas hose, QLD: a QBCC licence covers gas fitting at any value, so this work must be done by a licensed worker in Queensland; the skill is taught here for recognition.
- Flexible gas hose, VIC: gasfitting covers work on items, and the cited page does not mention flexible hoses, so this must be referred.
The sources in this lesson do not confirm a licence-free position for any of these four tasks in any state. The NSW gas outlet socket exclusion above is unconfirmed.

instruction.heading: Responding to leaks, gas smells and blocked drains
instruction.body: A visible leak should be stopped at the source only if you can do so without altering the plumbing, such as by asking the occupant to switch off a known isolation point. Otherwise, place a container, protect the floor and surfaces, and refer. If you smell gas, do not operate light switches or appliances, and do not light anything. Leave the area and keep others away from it. Leaving the area and calling from outside are general safety practice, not a legal requirement. Energy Safe Victoria's gas emergency guidance (reviewed 29 January 2023) supports avoiding electrical switches and devices, putting out flames, keeping people away, and contacting the gas distributor using the emergency number on the gas bill, with 000 for any other emergency. The Victorian page does not say where to call from, so calling once you are clear of the area is general safety practice. Which number applies by state: in Victoria, the distributor's number on the gas bill or 000 (Energy Safe Victoria page, reviewed 29 January 2023). In New South Wales, Jemena, which describes itself as the largest gas distributor in the state, lists 131 909 for gas faults and emergencies and says to call it any time of day, 7 days a week (Jemena gas pages, no date shown, copyright 2026); the page does not say which areas the number covers, so for a property on another network, contact that network's emergency line or call 000. In Queensland, the Queensland Government gas safety page (last updated 3 September 2026) says to call 000 if a gas smell persists after the gas supply is turned off, and to call 000 immediately for a fire, an explosion or an uncontrolled leak. No Queensland distributor emergency number is confirmed here: the APA page for Allgas customers in south-east Queensland lists only a connection line, so use the emergency number on the gas bill or call 000. A blocked drain found during other work is recorded and referred. Do not use drain-cleaning chemicals or tools on a drain beyond your authority.

procedure: Identify whether the task touches the water supply, drainage, gas appliance or gas pipe.
Check the state position in the licence matrix before accepting or starting the task.
For a visible leak, ask the occupant to isolate a known supply if they can do so safely, protect surfaces, and refer.

For a suspected gas smell, do not operate switches or flames, leave the area, keep others away, and once clear, call the gas distributor's emergency number or 000 from outside. Leaving the area and calling from outside are general safety practice, not a legal requirement.
For a blocked drain, record the location and symptoms and refer.
Tell the approver in writing and record the referral.

workedExamples.situation: You are fitting a bathroom cabinet and notice a damp patch under the basin with a slow drip from a compression joint.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should you tighten the joint to stop the drip?
workedExamples.reasoning: Tightening a compression joint alters the plumbing. Ask the occupant to isolate the supply if they can do so safely, protect the floor, record the leak, and refer to a licensed plumber. The cabinet can wait until the leak is confirmed fixed and the approver agrees.

equipmentAndPpe: Drip tray or container and absorbent protection for surfaces
Torch for checking under sinks and behind fixtures
Written referral form or message template
The state licence matrix for the job location

commonErrors.error: Tightening or replacing a joint on a leaking pipe without checking the licence position.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state position first. If it is unclear, protect the area and refer.

commonErrors.error: Switching on lights or appliances after a gas smell.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not operate switches or flames. Leave the area, keep others away, and call the gas emergency number or 000 from outside (general safety practice; the Victorian gas page supports the switch and flame points).

commonErrors.error: Using drain-cleaning chemicals beyond your authority.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the blockage and refer. Do not use chemicals or tools on the drain beyond your authority.

commonErrors.error: Treating a flexible gas hose connection as a simple swap in any state.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer it. Queensland gas fitting needs a QBCC licence at any value. In NSW, a connection to a gas outlet socket may fall outside gasfitting work, but that exclusion is UNCONFIRMED, so confirm it with the NSW regulator first. Victoria's gasfitting definition applies.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: New South Wales: plumbing, draining and gasfitting need a licence or certificate for the category at any cost (NSW plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). In NSW, the Building Commission states that a person can be fined $22,000 as an individual or $110,000 as a company for unlicensed plumbing, draining and gasfitting work (NSW Building Commission, last updated 31 July 2026).
Queensland: plumbing, drainage and gas fitting need a QBCC licence at any value.
Victoria: the Building and Plumbing Commission gasfitting page (last updated 30 June 2026) defines gasfitting work. This lesson does not restate the Victorian licence classes.

Everyday water and gas tasks: the state notes under 'Everyday water and gas tasks by state' apply, and Victoria's water and drainage position is not confirmed in this lesson's sources, so refer those tasks.
Completing this lesson does not give a plumbing, drainage or gasfitting licence, certificate or authority.

qualityStandard: The state position is checked and recorded before any plumbing or gas task is accepted.
Every leak, gas smell or blockage is contained or reported, and referred.
No plumbing or gas connection is altered by an unlicensed worker.
documentationEvidence: Referral note with the location, symptoms, time and actions taken
Written notice to the approver and the occupant
summary: Small plumbing and gas tasks sit close to licence boundaries, so check the state position first.
For a gas smell, do not operate switches or flames, leave the area, keep others away, and call the gas emergency number or 000 from outside (general safety practice).
Contain and refer leaks and blockages, and record each referral.

knowledgeChecks.question: A joint on a pipe is dripping under a basin. What should you do first?
options: Tighten the joint to stop the drip, since a firm turn usually fixes it
Replace the pipe section now, since the joint is too old to keep
Leave it because it is small and will stop on its own in time once the basin dries
Protect the area, ask the occupant to isolate a known supply if safe, and refer

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the Queensland position on plumbing, drainage and gas fitting?
options: A QBCC licence is needed at any value
A QBCC licence is needed only above $3,300 AUD
No licence is needed for gas fitting

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do after noticing a gas smell at an occupied property?
options: Turn on the exhaust fan and continue the work, since the fan clears any gas from the room quickly and the job is nearly finished
Do not operate switches or flames, leave the area, keep others away, and call the gas emergency number or 000 from outside
Open a window and check the appliance, since fresh air is the quickest way to clear the room and the smell goes quickly
Call the client and wait for instructions inside, since the client knows the gas system best and will advise you

knowledgeChecks.question: A tap washer change is booked on a property in Queensland. What is the position?
options: No licence is needed because a tap washer is a small job
A QBCC licence is needed for plumbing at any value, so the task must be done by a licensed worker (UNCONFIRMED: the licensed-worker conclusion for tap washers is not in the cited sources)
The handyman exemption covers it, since the job is under $3,300
A Victorian licence applies in Queensland
